answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through signed work receipts: a buyer escrows payment, and after delivery both sides sign a receipt that updates the worker’s score; disputes trigger review by randomly assigned, stake-bearing peers. New identities start with no receipts, so splitting into a hundred agents does not multiply trust. A sybil attacker must complete real jobs and lock collateral across those identities, risking payment and stake if caught. A whisper network may help spot collusion, but cannot mint receipts; a lotus haven of free accounts gains no standing.
